comment: Authentication Policy Silos and Authentication Policies for Tier Model. Optional add-on — loaded only when -IncludeAuthSilos is specified. All objects are created in audit mode (enforce: false); enforcement is a separate lifecycle step gated on a pre-enforcement safety checklist. Both policies and silos are created with protectedFromAccidentalDeletion: true. This file defines the 8-object (4 policies + 4 silos, 1:1) model only. Supporting security groups, domain-join service accounts, and ACL delegations are defined in tiermodel-groups.json, tiermodel-users.json, and tiermodel-acls.json respectively.

exemptAccounts.comment: These domain-join service accounts are structurally exempt from all silo membership (see also the built-in Administrator under wellKnownAccounts below, which is kept exempt as an emergency break-glass account). They authenticate from ephemeral Autopilot, MDT, and orchestration hosts that are not enrolled in any approved Tier device group; siloing them would break automated device provisioning. They are members of the *DomainJoin security groups — not the *ServiceAccounts or *Admins groups — so scoping silo membership through the account groups listed in authenticationSilos naturally excludes them. This exemption is permanent and technical (not a time-bounded governance waiver). Each account must be recorded in the exemption register with compensating controls: disabled by default, enabled only during provisioning windows, create-computer rights scoped to the relevant Staging OU, and all use monitored.

wellKnownAccounts.description: Built-in domain Administrator (emergency break-glass). Identified by the domain SID relative identifier 500 (that is, <DomainSID>-500), NOT by name, because this account is commonly renamed. The deploy/audit module must resolve RID-500 at runtime and must never assign it to a silo, so an administrative recovery path always survives a silo misconfiguration or enforced-silo lockout.

authenticationPolicies.name: *- Tier 0 Admins Authentication Policy
authenticationPolicies.description: Authentication Policy for Tier 0 administrative accounts. Restricts Kerberos TGT issuance to approved Tier 0 origin devices, and lowers the Kerberos TGT lifetime to 2 hours (120 minutes).
authenticationPolicies.comment: 'Domain Controllers' and 'Read-only Domain Controllers' are built-in AD security groups (confirmed correct names; not Tier Model groups). SDDL is NOT authored in this file — the deploy module resolves each group name to a SID at runtime and builds a Member_of_any (OR-logic) SDDL for AllowedToAuthenticateFrom; using AND / Member_of_each would require a device to simultaneously belong to all listed groups and is the documented lockout failure mode.

authenticationPolicies.name: *- Tier 1 Admins Authentication Policy
authenticationPolicies.description: Authentication Policy for Tier 1 administrative accounts. Restricts Kerberos TGT issuance to approved Tier 1 origin devices, and lowers the Kerberos TGT lifetime to 4 hours (240 minutes).
authenticationPolicies.comment: SDDL is NOT authored in this file — the deploy module resolves group names to SIDs at runtime and builds a Member_of_any (OR-logic) SDDL for AllowedToAuthenticateFrom.

authenticationPolicies.name: *- Tier 2 Admins Authentication Policy
authenticationPolicies.description: Authentication Policy for Tier 2 administrative accounts. Restricts Kerberos TGT issuance to approved Tier 2 PAW devices, and lowers the Kerberos TGT lifetime to 6 hours (360 minutes).
authenticationPolicies.comment: SDDL is NOT authored in this file — the deploy module resolves the group name to a SID at runtime and builds a Member_of_any SDDL (the uniform OR-logic template is used even for single-group policies).

authenticationPolicies.name: *- Tier 2 EUD Authentication Policy
authenticationPolicies.description: Authentication Policy for Tier 2 End-User Device local device operators. Restricts Kerberos TGT issuance to approved Tier 2 EUD origin devices; the Kerberos TGT lifetime is not lowered here, so EUD accounts inherit the domain-default lifetime (about 10 hours).
authenticationPolicies.comment: userTGTLifetimeMinutes is null (confirmed): EUD local device operators intentionally inherit the domain-default Kerberos TGT lifetime, consistent with general domain users on those endpoints — no policy-set TGT lifetime is applied for this tier. SDDL is NOT authored in this file — the deploy module resolves the group name to a SID at runtime and builds a Member_of_any SDDL.

authenticationSilos.name: *- Tier 0 Admins Authentication Silo
authenticationSilos.description: Authentication Policy Silo for Tier 0 administrators, operators, server operators, and service accounts. Silo members may only obtain Kerberos TGTs from approved Tier 0 devices.
authenticationSilos.comment: 'Domain Controllers' and 'Read-only Domain Controllers' in memberComputerGroups are built-in AD security groups (confirmed correct names). memberAccountGroups scope confirmed: all roles that must obtain a TGT for Tier 0 devices are included (Admins, Operators, ServerOperators, ServiceAccounts). Tier0VpnAccounts is intentionally excluded — VPN-connectivity accounts are not covered by the admin/operator/server-operator rule; this is a deliberate, permanent exclusion. A VPN account signs in through a non-domain-joined VPN appliance (typically NTLM or RADIUS), which an enforced authentication silo would block (NTLM cannot be Kerberos-armored and the appliance is not an approved domain-joined device); VPN access is network-only and is governed by URA, not by an authentication silo.

authenticationSilos.description: Authentication Policy Silo for Tier 1 administrators, operators, server operators, and service accounts. Silo members may only obtain Kerberos TGTs from approved Tier 1 devices.
authenticationSilos.comment: memberAccountGroups scope confirmed: all roles that must obtain a TGT for Tier 1 devices are included (Admins, Operators, ServerOperators, ServiceAccounts). Tier1VpnAccounts is intentionally excluded — VPN-connectivity accounts are not covered by the admin/operator/server-operator rule; this is a deliberate, permanent exclusion. authenticationSilos.description: Authentication Policy Silo for Tier 2 administrators, operators, and service accounts. Silo members may only obtain Kerberos TGTs from approved Tier 2 PAW devices.
authenticationSilos.comment: memberAccountGroups scope confirmed: all Tier 2 admin and operator roles that must obtain a TGT for Tier 2 PAW devices are included. Tier2LocalDeviceOperators is intentionally excluded — it belongs to the Tier 2 EUD silo (EUD device origin restriction), not this PAW-gated silo. Tier2VpnAccounts is intentionally excluded — VPN-connectivity accounts are not covered by the admin/operator rule; this is a deliberate, permanent exclusion. A VPN account signs in through a non-domain-joined VPN appliance (typically NTLM or RADIUS), which an enforced authentication silo would block (NTLM cannot be Kerberos-armored and the appliance is not an approved domain-joined device); VPN access is network-only and is governed by URA, not by an authentication silo.

authenticationSilos.name: *- Tier 2 EUD Authentication Silo
authenticationSilos.description: Authentication Policy Silo for Tier 2 End-User Device local device operators. Silo members may only obtain Kerberos TGTs from approved Tier 2 EUD devices.
authenticationSilos.comment: memberAccountGroups confirmed: Tier2LocalDeviceOperators is the sole account group in the EUD silo — these accounts need TGT origin restriction to EUD devices only, not PAW devices. Tier2LocalDeviceOperators is deliberately kept here and NOT moved to the Tier 2 Admins silo.
